# 4 Maccabees Chapter 10 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The Remaining Brothers and the Mother

---

**1** After the sixth had also died in blessed death after all his sufferings, the seventh and youngest was brought forward.

**2** The tyrant, feeling a kind of pity for the youngest because of his youth, called him close and urged him to have pity on himself and not to share in his brothers' supposed madness. He urged him to abandon the ancestral customs and live as a Greek.

**3** But the youth replied: I am the last of my brothers. I am not going to shame my brothers by refusing to share their suffering. I will resist you just as they did.

**4** What you are doing to me is not justice — it is cruelty. You are forcing forbidden food on me to make me betray God.

**5** No argument and no force can compel me, because I am governed by holy reason and I am worthy of my brothers.

**6** My brothers, having endured a brief agony, have now tasted of the ever-flowing life under God's covenant. But you, through the judgment of God, will receive just punishment for your arrogance.

**7** I, like my brothers, give up my body and life for the ancestral laws, praying to God to show mercy quickly to our people.

**8** And I pray that through me and my brothers the just wrath of God that has fallen on our whole nation may come to an end.

**9** As for me, I surrender my body and soul into God's hands, praying: O Lord, I am brought before you and I offer you my blood as a purification — let this be sufficient for our nation.

**10** When he had said this, they tortured him even more brutally than the others, furious at his contempt for them.

**11** But this was entirely consistent with his character, for he had been shaped by the same philosophy of courage as his brothers.

**12** And so, having committed his whole soul to God, he died nobly in his torments — another Eleazar.

**13** After all the brothers had died, their mother was last to be put to death.

**14** This mother of seven deserves praise surpassing every commendation given to human heroism — for she watched the murder of seven sons in the space of a single day and endured it with good courage because of her hope in God.

**15** She urged each one of them on in their ancestral language; filled with noble courage she fired her mother's heart with the strength of a warrior and said to them:

**16** I was a pure virgin and I never went beyond the walls of my father's house; and I did not know the pleasures of this world.

**17** I kept myself in chastity and I did not transgress God's commandments, and I know of no sin in my life.

**18** I say before my children: God has not given me another son; I know no other son, for he has taken from me each of those who might have kept his holy name alive.

**19** Therefore this is my supreme joy: having given birth to and raised these holy sons, I see not one of them separated from God's purpose.
